generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No parcel relation, legal-control conclusion, flood result, mining stability conclusion or environmental permission is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: The Article 4 direction-rule dataset currently contains zero rule records.
extra_examples.gate: Zero platform records must not be interpreted as no withdrawn permitted-development rights.

extra_examples.fact: Article 4 direction areas provide geometry for where a direction applies.
extra_examples.gate: A parcel must intersect the authoritative area and be linked to a current direction before applying control.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data models the legal direction separately from one or more geographic direction areas.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer parcel coverage from a direction record that lacks geometry.

extra_examples.ref: Article 4 start and end date gate
extra_examples.fact: The Article 4 specification includes start-date and end-date fields for legal effect periods.
extra_examples.gate: Expired or future directions must not be treated as current controls.

extra_examples.fact: ART4007 records several withdrawn permitted-development-right codes within an authoritative area.
extra_examples.gate: The legal meaning of each current code must be checked against the direction and proposal.

extra_examples.fact: The Great Yarmouth HMO area is an authoritative Article 4 geography linked to an HMO direction.
extra_examples.gate: Article 4 changes the planning-permission route; it is not an automatic refusal.

extra_examples.fact: York HMO area records withdrawn permitted-development-right code 3L.
extra_examples.gate: Exact parcel intersection and current direction scope are required.

extra_examples.fact: Barnet warns historic Article 4 classes have been translated to modern counterparts and older maps may be superseded.
extra_examples.gate: Use the current authority documentation rather than translated historic metadata alone.

extra_examples.ref: Class E to C3 CAZ control
extra_examples.fact: Westminster's direction removes specified Class E to C3 permitted-development rights in parts of the CAZ.
extra_examples.gate: Exact affected polygon and proposal use class must be verified.

extra_examples.ref: Class E to C3 outside-CAZ control
extra_examples.fact: A separate Westminster direction applies to specified town-centre areas outside the CAZ.
extra_examples.gate: Do not assume the CAZ direction and outside-CAZ direction share the same geography.

extra_examples.fact: EA Flood Zone 1 is land outside mapped Flood Zones 2 and 3 and has less than 0.1% annual river/sea flood probability under the planning-zone definition.
extra_examples.gate: Other flood sources and future climate risk may still require assessment.

extra_examples.fact: Flood Zone 2 covers defined medium-probability river/sea flood ranges and accepted recorded flood outlines.
extra_examples.gate: Use exact EA geometry and site-specific FRA triggers.

extra_examples.fact: Flood Zone 3 includes land with at least 1% annual river probability or 0.5% annual sea probability under the planning-zone definition.
extra_examples.gate: Functional-floodplain and vulnerability classifications still require separate assessment.

extra_examples.fact: Flood Zones plus Climate Change ignores benefits of existing flood defences.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat the layer as a defended residual-risk result.

extra_examples.fact: EA climate-change surface-water planning layers use UKCP18 RCP8.5 upper-end 2070s allowances.
extra_examples.gate: Scenario choice is strategic and not an individual property prediction.

extra_examples.fact: Present-day surface-water planning extents include a 3.3% annual-exceedance-probability scenario.
extra_examples.gate: Modelled extent must be checked against exact parcel geometry and local drainage evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Present-day surface-water planning extents include a 1% annual-exceedance-probability scenario.
extra_examples.gate: No individual-building flood conclusion is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: Present-day surface-water planning extents include a 0.1% annual-exceedance-probability scenario.
extra_examples.gate: Use as screening evidence only.

extra_examples.fact: EA present-day depth layers distinguish bands from up to 150mm through over 2300mm.
extra_examples.gate: Depth is modelled and not a guaranteed flood level at a property.

extra_examples.fact: EA climate-change depth layers combine the AEP scenarios with defined depth bands.
extra_examples.gate: Use exact location and FRA evidence; do not transfer depth values between parcels.

extra_examples.fact: EA explicitly states surface-water spatial-planning datasets are not suitable for determining whether an individual property will flood.
extra_examples.gate: Property-level risk requires additional evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Source Protection Zones protect public potable groundwater abstractions by screening potentially polluting activities.
extra_examples.gate: Zone membership is a regulatory/planning input, not blanket prohibition.

extra_examples.fact: EA defines the inner protection zone using groundwater travel-time concepts around abstractions.
extra_examples.gate: Use current EA geometry and exact activity risk assessment.

extra_examples.fact: Groundwater safeguard zones identify locations where additional pollution-control measures are needed around public supplies.
extra_examples.gate: Exact proposal type and pollutant pathway determine the development implication.

extra_examples.fact: Groundwater safeguard zones often build from SPZ2 but may differ after additional pollution assessment.
extra_examples.gate: Do not substitute one geometry for the other.

extra_examples.fact: The current groundwater-vulnerability dataset supersedes older EA 100k vulnerability data.
extra_examples.gate: Prefer the newer digital dataset for current screening.

extra_examples.fact: Aquifer designation identifies Principal and multiple Secondary aquifer classes plus Unproductive Strata.
extra_examples.gate: Aquifer class alone does not establish groundwater impact or planning outcome.

extra_examples.fact: BGS notes its older 1:100,000 aquifer-vulnerability maps date from the late 1980s/early 1990s.
extra_examples.gate: Use current digital EA/BGS groundwater datasets where available.

extra_examples.ref: Coal Development High Risk Area trigger
extra_examples.fact: The Development High Risk Area combines recorded mine entries, shallow workings, hazards, mine-gas sites, fissures and former surface mining.
extra_examples.gate: Exact parcel intersection and site-specific CMRA are required.

extra_examples.fact: MRA guidance says mine-entry locations should be established by intrusive investigation when relevant to layout or development quantum.
extra_examples.gate: Mapped approximate features are insufficient for final layout decisions.

extra_examples.fact: CMRA evidence may need to demonstrate no-build zones or other layout responses around mining features.
extra_examples.gate: No no-build zone is inferred without exact site investigation.

extra_examples.ref: Building over mine entries avoidance policy
extra_examples.fact: MRA guidance says building over or close to mine entries should be avoided wherever possible, even after capping.
extra_examples.gate: Exact influence zone and engineering response are site-specific.

extra_examples.fact: MRA expects the final CMRA to identify competent authors/reviewers and not be submitted as a draft or issue-for-comment version.
extra_examples.gate: Draft or unsigned reports are not treated as final evidence.

extra_examples.fact: CMRA guidance expects individual and cumulative effects of coal-mining legacy risks to be assessed.
extra_examples.gate: No stability score is inferred from one isolated mining feature.

extra_examples.fact: MRA says professional advice may change when new information, scheme changes or policy changes arise.
extra_examples.gate: Time-stamp and revalidate advice before relying on it.

extra_examples.fact: Hazardous-substances consent controls the presence of specified substances and may be required separately from planning permission.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat planning permission as proof hazardous-substances consent exists.

extra_examples.fact: HSE states consent is required where specified hazardous substances are present at or above defined limits.
extra_examples.gate: Exact substance and quantity must be established.

extra_examples.fact: Applications are made to the hazardous substances authority, usually the local planning authority, rather than directly to HSE.
extra_examples.gate: Procedure is not consent status.

extra_examples.fact: HSE smart-form guidance warns incomplete hazardous-substance applications can delay decisions.
extra_examples.gate: Submission does not equal valid or granted consent.

extra_examples.ref: Local green space zero-data fail-closed control
extra_examples.fact: Planning Data currently has zero local-green-space records and no collection attempt.
extra_examples.gate: Use local-plan/policies-map evidence; zero platform data is not zero designation.

extra_examples.fact: Built-up areas are ONS statistical geography rather than development allocations.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use built-up-area membership as permission or capacity evidence.

extra_examples.fact: The Derby built-up-area entity provides authoritative ONS geometry.
extra_examples.gate: Exact geometry remains statistical context only.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data combines GLA/borough Central Activities Zone data and notes some MHCLG-created provenance.
extra_examples.gate: Current GLA and borough policies maps should control exact parcel assignment.

extra_examples.fact: CAZ00000004 carries detailed polygon geometry but quality is recorded as 'some'.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat it as definitive without current GLA/borough cross-check.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's smoke-control consideration remains research-stage and flags restrictive/unclear licensing around underlying mapped data.
extra_examples.gate: No parcel geometry or current smoke-control status is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: The High Weald AONB entity supplies mapped geometry but records quality as 'some'.
extra_examples.gate: Cross-check the current authoritative Natural England/National Landscape boundary before parcel scoring.
